name: Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone
overview: Thyroid-Stimulating Hormone is a health topic that clinicians and patients frequently discuss during care planning in India and worldwide. Key considerations include thyroid-stimulating hormone (also known as thyrotropin, thyrotropic hormone, or abbreviated tsh) is a pituitary hormone that stimulates the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine (t4), and then triiodothyronine (t3) which stimulates the metabolism of almost every tissue in the body; it is a glycoprotein hormone produced by thyrotrope cells in the anterior pituitary gland, which regulates the endocrine function of the thyroid. This summary is educational and should be paired with professional medical evaluation.
